metadata.title: Fine Print
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Course pitch film, not a channel episode (INFO 7375 Final Project Pitch Film, 2-4 min): it opens on the hesitant writer, has no verdict card, and drops the Your Turn composer to keep the runtime under four minutes. The terms card is dropped too: GATE T measured its fixed-size definition text at 40 px, under the 41 px floor, so each term is defined in the narration where it is first used (show-tell law 3). The spoken outro stays but is our own drawn beat with the student's name: the toolkit's ClaudeTitleOutro hard-codes the handle @NikBearBrown, and the assignment says to narrate as yourself and not to use the instructor's name, persona or credit line.
metadata.audience: a hiring manager or ML engineer reviewing a new-grad ML/AI engineer's portfolio; the course TAs

skin_warnings: BIDEA: palette=claude but the cold open is 'BrutalistHesitantWriter' — COLD OPEN LAW wants ClaudeComposerAsk
BOUT: palette=claude but the outro is 'un-annotated' — OUTRO LAW wants ClaudeTitleOutro

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Suketh Produtoor. I'm an international student on F-1, looking for new-grad machine learning roles. The question isn't only whether a company sponsors. It's whether the posting even fits me.

show.event: backspaces 'company sponsor me' -> 'posting even fit me'

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the company-level question and corrects it to the posting-level one.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Earlier this term, Claude Code and I built a recipe for the course's job-search engine, the Reallocation Engine. It checks a company's sponsor record, its past work-visa filings, at the role level. Claude wrote the code; I chose the rules and ran the checks. Its thirty-six tests still pass.

shot.visual_intent: An evidence binder (the A3 recipe) opens; check marks land beside it as the tests are named.
shot.motion_claim: An evidence binder (the A3 recipe) opens; check marks land beside it as the tests are named.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Then it screened eight real postings by title and company record, for Arjun Rao, a fictional applicant with no work history on file. Read in full, six asked for two to twelve-plus years of experience, or excluded new graduates. An AI reviewer read them, Claude re-checked, and I held all eight.

shot.visual_intent: Eight posting pages in two rows; a scan passes over them and six get a dark marker; '6 of 8' lands; a hold bar lies across all eight.
shot.motion_claim: Eight posting pages in two rows; a scan passes over them and six get a dark marker; '6 of 8' lands; a hold bar lies across all eight.

beats.narration_text: A relevant title and a sponsor record are useful signals. But the posting itself can change the decision. So I will build Fine Print: an agent that will read each posting, quote the sentence behind every requirement, and stop for my approval before anything reaches my shortlist.

shot.visual_intent: The inspection lamp swings over a posting page; fine-print lines lift off the page as quote slips.
shot.motion_claim: The inspection lamp swings over a posting page; fine-print lines lift off the page as quote slips.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Every requirement it finds will need its sentence, word for word. Code will check that the sentence really is in the posting. If it isn't, the requirement gets thrown out.

shot.visual_intent: A quote slip rides through the checkpoint scanner and gets a check; a second slip fails and drops off.
shot.motion_claim: A quote slip rides through the checkpoint scanner and gets a check; a second slip fails and drops off.

beats.narration_text: What could sink it: a real quote, read the wrong way. Say a posting says five years preferred, and the agent records required. The quote check would still pass. So preferred, required, and either-or rules will stay apart, and anything unclear will stop at me.

shot.visual_intent: Constructed example: a slip reading '5 yrs preferred' passes the scanner with a check, but the reading 'required' is ringed and the slip is turned aside to the review desk.
shot.motion_claim: Constructed example: a slip reading '5 yrs preferred' passes the scanner with a check, but the reading 'required' is ringed and the slip is turned aside to the review desk.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, with the voice carrying the explanation. The negative space is the style, so only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: A requirement also needs the applicant's documented background beside it. I have about two and a half years at Amazon and six months at Vertex, so two years required needs a comparison, not a guess. The repo will use a fictional profile; mine stays private.

shot.visual_intent: Comparison trays: the requirement in one tray, a profile card in the other; a balance line draws between them.
shot.motion_claim: Comparison trays: the requirement in one tray, a profile card in the other; a balance line draws between them.

beats.narration_text: It will run as a loop: fetch a public posting from an allowed job board, read it, check the sponsor record, log what it found. It will stop when the list is done or the budget runs out. It will read, and never apply, email, or log in.

shot.visual_intent: A permission gate lifts for a posting (read), budget slots empty one token at a time; a crossed 'apply' stays shut.
shot.motion_claim: A permission gate lifts for a posting (read), budget slots empty one token at a time; a crossed 'apply' stays shut.

beats.narration_text: That's the human gate: nothing will reach my shortlist until I approve it, and the record will keep exactly what I saw. A value the model proposed will still say source: model, and my approval will be recorded beside it, as its own field. My earlier prototype labelled those as mine.

shot.visual_intent: The approval stamp presses onto the reviewed page; a tag reads 'source: model', and a second tag 'review: approved' is added beside it; neither replaces the other.
shot.motion_claim: The approval stamp presses onto the reviewed page; a tag reads 'source: model', and a second tag 'review: approved' is added beside it; neither replaces the other.

beats.narration_text: I checked graduate ML descriptions from Qualcomm and TikTok on LinkedIn. Both separate minimum and preferred qualifications; neither accessible description states sponsorship. Fine Print will preserve those distinctions, attach checked source quotes, and keep missing sponsorship evidence marked unknown.

shot.visual_intent: Left: the two LinkedIn postings, each split into minimum and preferred blocks, with an empty sponsorship slot (real, my check). Right: Fine Print's report with quote slips and one slip flagged unknown (sketch).
shot.motion_claim: Left: the two LinkedIn postings, each split into minimum and preferred blocks, with an empty sponsorship slot (real, my check). Right: Fine Print's report with quote slips and one slip flagged unknown (sketch).

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager or an ML engineer. In the first minute, they'll run one command with no API key, which replays recorded model outputs, and read the report: each posting, each requirement beside its sentence, and my decision.

shot.visual_intent: A release parcel (the repository) opens and a report page slides out with three quote rows.
shot.motion_claim: A release parcel (the repository) opens and a report page slides out with three quote rows.

beats.narration_text: It should prove I can build an agent whose claims can be checked. I'll label real postings by hand, set a held-out group aside before tuning, and count two mistakes separately: clearing a posting I don't qualify for, and excluding one I do.

beats.narration_text: It will never apply for me. The first piece will be one loop over one public posting, with the quote check, and a test that fails if a quote changes by a single word.

shot.visual_intent: The task queue hands over one task (one posting); a test light goes from check to cross when one word changes.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. I already have production ML from Amazon, data checks with human sign-off from Vertex, and AgentOS, my open-source project with budget limits and a kill switch. New to me: reading a requirement without changing what it means, and testing extraction and interpretation separately.

shot.motion_claim: A stack of skill pages ('have'); one new blank page arrives beside it ('new').

beats.narration_text: Today there's the recipe, its passing tests, the eight-posting finding, and an open pull request. Not yet: the agent, the quote check, the evaluation. Those I will build.
